To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) The ionization of adenine-containing oligonucleotides is a one-photon process for (dAdt)10(dAdt)10, (dT)10 and (dT)20 and a two-photon process for dA, (dA)(10), (dA)(20), (dT)(10) and (dT)(20); (b) the quantum yield for one- and two-photion ionization is higher for (dAd)10

the quantum yield for one and two-photon absorption of adenine-containing oligonucleotides in aqueous solution is higher than that of adenine and that the quantum yield of the one-photon ionizing absorption is higher for the single helix than for the double helix.

the ionization potentials of the DNA single- and double-stranded helices are lower than that of the monomer, and that the ionization potential of the single helix is lower than that corresponding to the double helix.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of DNA damage by ionization induced by UV light.
the ionization of DNA oligomers by one- and two-photons at the wavelength of 266 nm.
a better understanding of the role of the DNA base sequence on the ionization of oligomers by UV light.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the ionization of the double helix is more difficult than that of the single strand, the ionization of (dAd)10(dAd)10 is easier than that of (Ad)20(dT), and the ionization of adenine runs is easier than that for adenine-thymidine runs.

the ionization of the adenine bases in the oligonucleotides is favored by the stacking of the bases and by their organization in helices, and that the ionization is more efficient for the adenine bases located at the ends of the oligonucleotide sequences.
the ionization potential of the adenine bases in the oligomers is lowered by the organization in helix and that the degree of lowering depends on the sequence of the oligomer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ionization potential of the DNA double helices depends on the base composition, the sequence and the base pairing.
the quantum yield for one and two-photon absorption is strongly dependent on the base composition and sequence.
the one-photon ionizing potential of DNA single and duplexes depends on the sequence and the base composition, but is always higher than that of dA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
one-photon ionizing laser pulses can be used to induce ionization in oligonucleotides and that this ionization is sensitive to the base sequence and to the pairing of the oligomers.
the DNA double helix is more difficult to ionize than the single strand.
the ionization potential of the DNA single helix is lower than that expected from the ionization potential values of the monomers, in agreement with the recent theoretical predictions.
